chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a female slave shared between two men who had both manumitted her, then one of them made her private part permissible for his partner. He said: 'It is permissible for him, and whichever of them dies before the other, half of her becomes free from the side of the one who died, and the other half remains manumitted [in the share of the survivor].'

I said: 'What if you see that the survivor among them wants to have sexual intercourse with her? Is that for him?' He said: 'No, unless he confirms her manumission and marries her with her consent, just as he intended.'
I said: 'Hasn't half of her become free? She has owned half of her neck [body], and the other half belongs to the survivor among them?' He said: 'Yes.'
I said: 'If she makes her master permissible regarding her private part and makes it permissible for him?' He said: 'That is not permissible.'
I said: 'And why is it not permissible for her, just as you permitted the one who had half of her when he made her private part permissible for his partner in her?'

'Indeed, a free woman does not give away her private part, nor lend it, nor make it permissible. But she has a day from herself, and the one who manumitted her has a day. So if he wishes to marry her for something as a gift in the day that she owns herself, he may enjoy her for something, little or much.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّ فَرْجَهَا: made her private part permissible (for sexual use)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sexual relations with a partially manumitted shared slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudence of *kitabah* (partial manumification) in a shared slave, establishing that upon one owner's death, his share of freedom is immediately realized, creating a dual-status entity. Al-Tusi uses this to distinguish between the right of possession and the right of chastity, noting that while the survivor retains ownership, he cannot exercise sexual rights without full manumification and marriage, as a free woman cannot simply 'gift' her chastity. The ruling further permits temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) as a valid mechanism for the survivor to enjoy her, highlighting the flexibility of Shia marital law in managing shared property rights.
